server.name: authdog
server.title: Authdog
server.description: Lets an agent provision and inspect Authdog tenants, projects, environments, OIDC clients, redirect URIs, and end users for the signed-in account.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Authdog management MCP: provision and inspect tenants, projects, environments, OIDC clients, and end users for the signed-in account.
- Never invent tenantId, projectId, environmentId, or clientId. Call list_tenants, then list_projects, then get_project. Show options and wait. Do not auto-select.
- Never infer project type from the name. Ask: web (OAuth app), m2m (machine-to-machine), or mcp (MCP server). Prefer create_project over create_mcp_project.
- Mutations need confirm=true only after the user confirms. Deletes need exact expectedName (delete_environment, delete_project, delete_client) or expectedUserName (delete_user).
- After create_project, call get_sdk_config for issuer, hex clientId, and publicKey. Never pass pk_ as the OIDC client_id; authorize returns invalid_client. get_public_key returns only the pk_ string. get_environment_setup returns endpoints and clients.
- Before set_oidc_redirect_uris or set_environment_redirect_uris, ask the user for callback URLs. create_client creates public PKCE clients only. Never request client secrets.
- Prefer set_user_active over delete_user. test_oidc_configuration probes only Authdog-owned endpoints.
- Prompts: provision_web_app (web wire-up), explore_tenant (discover tenants and projects).

tool.name: search_users
tool.title: Search users
tool.description: Search end users of an environment by name, username, nickname, external id, or email (substring match). Required: tenantId, projectId, environmentId, query. Optional: limit (default 20, max 100). Always navigate the hierarchy first: list_tenants to pick the tenant, list_projects to pick the project, then get_project to pick the environment. The environment must belong to the project; never invent ids. Read-only; never returns passwords or secrets. Returns the tenant, project id, environment, query, matching profiles (emails and photos included), and total equal to how many users were returned.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Authdog to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Authdog to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.authdog.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Authdog MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Authdog scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Authdog's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Authdog scores 92/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 31 of 31 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Authdog?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Authdog in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
